Standard: The air vehicle can maintain control during a carrier bolter, with flying qualities no worse than qualitative Level 2, including maintaining wingtips within the foul lines of the landing area. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis of shore-based and shipboard carrier bolter, while maintaining wingtips within the carrier foul lines (e.g., landing area) and control, within adequate tolerances, of pitch attitude, AOA, bank angle, heading, pitch rate, and specific excess energy, to determine needed aerodynamic and ground handling control power and bandwidth, sink off deck performance, and specific excess energy needed to complete the mission task, including 6-DOF simulations for automatic control modes, for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and landing area dimensions, ship departure patterns, approach speed, flight path angle, WOD magnitude and direction, steady and turbulence carrier airwake and ship motion effects, ship speed and turn rate, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment). Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation of land-based and shipboard carrier bolter, while maintaining wingtips within the carrier foul lines or land-based representations, as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section, including 6-DOF simulations for automatic control modes, for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and landing area dimensions, ship departure patterns, approach speed, flight path angle, WOD magnitude and direction, steady and turbulence carrier airwake and ship motion effects, ship speed and turn rate, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct shore-based bolter tests as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section for nominal and critical combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and landing area dimensions, ship departure patterns, approach speed, flight path angle, headwind and crosswind conditions from minimum to maximum shore-based WOD equivalent, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment).
  (3) Flight test: Conduct shipboard bolter tests as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section, while maintaining wingtips within the carrier foul lines (e.g., landing area), for nominal and critical combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and landing area dimensions, ship departure patterns, approach speed, flight path angle, WOD magnitude and direction, steady and turbulence carrier airwake and ship motion effects, ship speed and turn rate, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment).
